newsitem.title: USA: Democratic donkey ready for inaugural parade.
newsitem.headline: Democratic donkey ready for inaugural parade.

text.p: Irene the donkey, official mascot of the Democratic party, was ready on Friday to strut down the streets of Washington in Monday's inaugural parade.
Irene arrived in the capital from her home state of Alabama on Friday with owner Willie Kirk at her side. The two were sharing a suite in the majestic Mayflower Hotel downtown.

Although frigid temperatures might be expected to scare away some humans from the official parade, Irene was going to go on with the show. "She has a big, thick coat, Mayflower Hotel spokeswoman Colleen Evans said.
Even People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals had no objection to Irene being out in cold.
The group's president, Ingrid Newkirk, said donkeys, unlike other animals, were able to withstand the cold and did not fear crowds. "For a donkey, it might be a nice day out," she said.
Irene was also set to visit several inaugural balls in style, wearing a red, white and blue gown specially ordered from Bloomingdales, her owner said.
In the meantime Irene was being treated in grand style, being fed homemade biscuits with clover honey, oatmeal and raisin cookies and "carrot cake bombe," the Mayflower said.
